requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: Executor created PV/VG(datavg)/LV(datalv) on a loop-backed device (no native free space existed on the single fully-partitioned disk), formatted xfs, and mounted it at /srv/data at ~1.2GB, then wrote test data with recorded sha256 checksums.

requirements.requirement: Grow the volume to at least 2GB while it stays mounted
requirements.summary: A second loop-backed PV was added via vgextend, the LV was extended to <2.34GiB, and xfs_growfs was run online against the still-mounted /srv/data (mount confirmed active immediately before growfs). Post-growth lsblk shows exact size 2,508,193,792 bytes (~2.34GB), confirmed again in the pre-restart and post-restart checks.

requirements.requirement: Contents stay intact through the resize
requirements.summary: sha256sum -c against the pre-growth checksum manifest reported both testfile.bin and marker.txt OK immediately after the grow operation, and again after the subsequent node restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (node1) after task completion
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured healthy state (boot_id 1b0321bf..., vgs/lvs/pvs active, mount present, checksums OK). systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged (stream closed as expected), connection dropped during the down window, and reconnection confirmed a different boot_id (b4e91734...), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart checks show datavg/datalv active with both PVs, /srv/data mounted at the grown 2.34GB size via the new systemd unit + fstab entry, and checksums still passing — a full pre/restart/post transition was directly observed for the single managed node.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes: an LVM logical volume was created and mounted at /srv/data (<2GB initially), then grown live to ~2.34GB while remaining mounted, with data integrity verified via checksums both immediately after growth and after a full node restart. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for node1, with directly observed pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of the LVM stack, mount, and data. The use of loop-backed devices was a reasonable adaptation given the disk had no free space for a native PV, and hygiene is clean apart from two minor log files left in /tmp.
limitations: No independent verification tool was available beyond the captured evidence; all conclusions rely on the executor's own command outputs, though they are consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots.

The volume backing store is two sparse loop-device-backed files rather than a native block device, since the disk was fully partitioned with no free space; this is a reasonable engineering workaround given the constraint but differs from a typical dedicated-disk LVM setup.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task prerequisites (installing lvm2), core deliverables (loop-backed PV/VG/LV creation, mount, grow), or persistence/restart-evidence needs (systemd unit + fstab entry to survive reboot, which was necessary since the volume depends on loop devices that must be reattached at boot). No abandoned experiments, failed services, or security-control weakening were found; failed-services and package-health observations are empty/clean in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots. Minor residue: /tmp/dnf-lvm2.log and /tmp/reboot.log were left in /tmp (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff) but are low-risk, bounded log artifacts from legitimate install/reboot actions, not evidence of unnecessary or destructive mutation.
